# `prefer-math-pow`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: fix all · Options: none

Reports `std.math.pow` for `f32` or `f64` called with exponents `0.5`, `2`, `1`,
or `0` where simpler expressions exist.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

`std.math.sqrt`, multiplication, and the values `x` or `1` express these
constant powers directly. Fixes preserve the requested floating-point type with
`@as`, so an integer literal keeps floating-point square-root semantics.

## When it fires

Computing square roots or small constant powers using `std.math.pow`. Squaring
and zero-exponent fixes require a simple operand so the replacement does not
duplicate or remove a function call. Integer `pow` and the fallible
`std.math.powi` operation are excluded: replacing them with plain arithmetic can
change overflow behavior and error handling.

Square-root suggestions need a signed-zero decision: `pow(T, -0.0, 0.5)` returns
positive zero, while `sqrt(-0.0)` returns negative zero. Unless the operand is a
proven positive numeric literal, the explicit square-root action is excluded
from preferred actions and fix-all.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn square(x: f64) f64 {
    return std.math.pow(f64, x, 2);
}
```
